event.detail: Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333. event.summary: A surviving old agent can be reaped by a guarded Delete after startup retirement fails
event.detail:
Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333.

TLDR: if the upgrade cannot end an old terminal, Farhelm still treats its session as interrupted. A later Delete that did not warn about stopping a live agent can reap that surviving agent and its unsaved work. This follows from source; it was not reproduced.

Details: this patch removes the tmux-specific probe and live-pane roots in teardown.rs:320-345. The replacement startup path core/old_terminals.rs:179-200,267-277 can leave an old server alive after an ordinary connect/identity/termination failure; core.rs:6675-6679 nevertheless finds no terminal for every old-kind row, and core.rs:6808-6820 converts a formerly Running row to TerminalEnded/Interrupted. terminal_less_launch_may_be_live at core.rs:5197-5218 only guards LastOutcome::Launching, not Interrupted. still_alive_for_delete at core.rs:13312-13355 therefore finds no runtime to probe and no host launch records for an old tmux-only session; NothingAlive can pass. handlers.rs:1253-1279 calls that guard then teardown. teardown.rs:411-415 requires the portable sweep for the missing-terminal entry and :531-540 invokes WholeSession. sweep.rs:251-258,421-445 claims surviving processes carrying that session's marker, so on a later successful process-table read it can stop the old live agent. This route needs an old marked agent to survive the startup failure, then a user Delete from the interrupted display. It needs no second simultaneous fault and no pid reuse. Old-server startup failure is an explicitly accepted product residual, discussed below.

Contract and proposed drop: SPEC.md, Lifecycle operations, lines 2048-2061 says a destructive confirmation authorizes only its displayed state and a Delete whose prompt said nothing alive must refuse if the agent is running. However SPEC.md, Terminal experience, lines 3004-3016 explicitly says: 'A failure to end the server or to stop what ran there is logged and never stops the supervisor from starting; those sessions are treated as ended all the same, accepting that a Restart could then start a second agent beside one still running.' SPEC_impl.md, Terminal substrate: private tmux server, lines 2919-2924 likewise says: 'A failure anywhere is logged and never fatal (the maintainer chose to start anyway and treat old sessions as ended, accepting that a Restart could then start a second agent beside one still running)'. proposed_drop: the explicit instruction to treat these sessions as ended appears to accept this consequence of failed old-terminal retirement; retain this record for the independent highest-drop check because the text specifically names duplicate Restart rather than an unconfirmed later Delete. Do not infer that the general rare-fault exception alone authorizes it.

Suggested bucket: highest/security or loss of work if retained, because the established route stops a live agent beyond what the ended-state Delete warned about, including unsaved agent work. Could-be-highest: yes. Confidence: confirmed source route conditional on the explicitly supported startup-failure state; whether its acceptance covers this Delete is a contract interpretation, not an unsettled source premise. possible_cover: none; no coverage sources consulted. Material caveats: legacy tmux sessions only; no issue established for ordinary terminal-host sessions. The upgrade deliberately tries to end old agents anyway; the concern is the later action's consent boundary after that end failed, not the authorized upgrade retirement itself. No runtime tests or reproductions performed.

Host-record origin and legacy creation metadata are being checked further in this synthesis; no evidence so far that old tmux-only creation minted .host records.

SPEC.md:3014-3016 says failure to end the server or what ran there does not prevent startup and "those sessions are treated as ended all the same, accepting that a Restart could then start a second agent beside one still running." The necessary premise is an old marked agent actually left alive by that bounded cleanup; neither any logged startup failure nor any early server error implies a survivor.
